findings.source_quote: Σὺ πρῶτον εἰπὲ τί σοι δοκεῖ τὸ ἀγαθόν; ἢ καὶ τὸ δίκαιον;
findings.english_quote: You first tell us what seems to you good, and what just.
findings.issue: The draft replaces the second question’s disjunctive/additive ἢ καί, ‘or also,’ with an unqualified ‘and.’ It also makes the request for a conception of goodness and justice less explicit than the substantival Greek.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: ‘You tell me first: what do you think goodness is? Or justice, too?’ Preserve the alternative-question structure. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ὡς σοὶ δοκεῖ αὐτὸς ὢν ἐπυθόμην ποιήσομαι τὰς· ἀποκρίσεις.
findings.english_quote: I will give the answers as you wish, although I was the one who asked.
findings.issue: The contextual interpretation is defensible, but the smooth English conceals the irregular juxtaposition of participial ὢν and finite ἐπυθόμην. The draft supplies no disclosure of that construction. The selected print reads ὢν, not the relative pronoun ὃς that would more directly support ‘the one who asked.’
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining that the English interprets the printed construction contextually, with Peter answering despite having himself asked. If ὃς for ὢν is mentioned, identify it strictly as a proposed correction, not the supplied reading. The printed punctuation in ‘τὰς· ἀποκρίσεις’ is not grounds for an OCR diagnosis or a verification block.

findings.source_quote: τῷ μὲν πᾶσιν παρέχειν, διαφόροις δὲ χαρίζεσθαι
findings.english_quote: in providing for all but granting different gifts
findings.issue: The draft selects a gifts/instrumental interpretation of διαφόροις without explaining it. The dative can instead identify recipients: ‘to different people,’ or potentially ‘to the distinguished/worthy.’ This materially affects whether the contrast concerns the gifts or their recipients; the Greek does not simply print an accusative object meaning ‘different gifts.’
findings.suggested_revision: Explicitly compare the draft with ‘by providing for everyone but granting favors to different recipients.’ If retaining ‘different gifts,’ explain the instrumental construal and its contextual support, and preserve the recipient interpretation in a note. If choosing recipients, explain the alternatives ‘different’ and ‘distinguished/worthy.’ Any revised wording and notes require fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ μακρόθυμον ταύτη μᾶλλον, εἰ ἁμαρτωλοῖς μὲν μετανοοῦσιν χαρίζεται τὰ ἁμαρτήματα, εὖ πράξασιν δὲ καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον ὑπογράφει.
findings.english_quote: and all the more patient in this way: he forgives sinners their sins when they reorient and promises eternal life also to those who have acted well.
findings.issue: The conditional εἰ is not represented. The colon turns the conditional argument into an unqualified assertion about forgiveness and eternal life. The draft’s ‘when’ represents the participle μετανοοῦσιν; it does not account for εἰ.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: ‘and all the more patient in this respect, if he forgives the sins of sinners who reorient and also promises eternal life to those who have acted well.’ Review the revised sentence afresh, including the scope of the condition.

findings.source_quote: ὅστις κατὰ ἀριθμὸν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, οἳ εἰσῆλθον εἰς Αἴγυπτον (οἵ εἰσιν ἑβδομήκοντα), καὶ πρὸς τὰ ὅρια τῶν ἐθνῶν περιγράψας γλώσσαις ἑβδομήκοντα
findings.english_quote: In accordance with the number of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt, who are seventy, and marking out the nations’ boundaries by seventy languages
findings.issue: The contextual delineation is defensible, but the English silently makes ‘the nations’ boundaries’ the object of ‘marking out.’ In the supplied construction, τὰ ὅρια belongs to the prepositional phrase πρὸς τὰ ὅρια, while περιγράψας has an unexpressed object. The attachment of the number and boundary phrases is not explained by the existing note about retaining ‘Israel.’
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining the elliptical object and the attachment adopted. Compare the draft with a more source-transparent formulation such as ‘having marked out divisions by seventy languages, in accordance with the number … and in relation to the nations’ boundaries.’ If retaining the draft, explain why the boundaries are understood as the contextual object. This is an interpretive construction issue, not evidence of unreadable print or an additional lacuna.

findings.source_quote: ἀπὸ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ πάντων κυρίου
findings.english_quote: from the Son, the Lord of all
findings.issue: The appositional interpretation is contextually defensible, especially after the Son has already been called ‘Lord,’ but it is not the only material construction. The consecutive genitives also permit ‘from the Son of the Lord of all.’ The draft does not disclose this alternative or explain its choice.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the appositional interpretation only with a note preserving ‘from the Son of the Lord of all’ as the alternative and explaining that the earlier designation of the Son as Lord favors the chosen attachment. Review the amended passage and note afresh; the existence of this alternative does not itself require blocking.

findings.source_quote: εἰ δὲ ὑπονοίᾳ αὐτοῦ κεχράτησαι ὡς ἀληθοῦς
findings.english_quote: But if you are held by its supposition as true
findings.issue: The draft understandably interprets κεχράτησαι as a passive holding verb, but it does not disclose the apparent spelling irregularity relative to the regular κεκράτησαι. Its English is also unnecessarily obscure: ‘its supposition as true’ does not clearly express a supposition concerning the account’s truth. The verified supplied spelling must not be silently regularized or labeled an OCR error.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose ‘But if you have been gripped by the supposition that it is true,’ with a source-quoted note identifying κεχράτησαι as the supplied reading and explaining the contextual passive interpretation. Identify κεκράτησαι only as a proposed regularization, not verified replacement text. Preserve the already adequate four-dot gap and its source-quoted nonrestoration note unchanged. The proposed wording and disclosure require fresh review.
